entries.text: EvoOntology separates its versioned ontology into content, schema, and tool layers so semantic records, their object model, and runtime exposure can evolve independently.
The ontology is exposed through MCP browse and resolve tools while only a compact manifest is placed in the prompt, allowing selective runtime retrieval instead of full-context injection.
entries.locator: Method > Agent-First Ontology-Layer Architecture > Tool Layer

entries.text: The evolution loop analyzes historical trajectories, attributes a failure signature to content, tool, or schema, and proposes a localized single-level patch with an expected behavioral effect.
entries.locator: Method > Trajectory-Grounded Ontology Evolution > Trajectory Attribution and Localized Intervention

entries.text: A candidate ontology patch is retained only when paired evaluation against its parent on the same validation set, decoding settings, and interaction budget reaches a required improvement margin.
entries.locator: Method > Trajectory-Grounded Ontology Evolution > Backbone-Conditional Paired Validation, Equation 2

entries.text: The reported ablation found that removing the acceptance gate caused the largest performance drop, followed by removing failure attribution.
entries.locator: Analyses > Ablation Study on Evolution Loop > Table 5

entries.text: Static prompt injection of the semantic layer was inconsistent and sometimes reduced performance, while selective tool access produced stable gains in the reported benchmarks.
